minutes.headline: Finance Committee held off spending free cash on capital and planned a debt subcommittee; no budget votes
minutes.summary: The committee discussed COVID-era uncertainty over state aid, school reopening costs, unemployment costs, and whether to defer capital spending and use free cash. It reviewed the debt service spreadsheet and agreed to form a small debt subcommittee, to be charged on June 11. Earlier minutes were taken up and the meeting adjourned.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no budget votes and held off committing free cash to capital spending while COVID-era state aid, school and unemployment costs stay uncertain.
The committee agreed to form a small debt subcommittee, to be charged at its June 11 meeting.
After reviewing the debt service spreadsheet, members said they want borrowing and credit rating scenarios, since debt service is projected to rise in a later year.
The committee will scrub the capital plan again at its next meeting for items that must be spent before mid-November.
Staff expect CARES Act and FEMA reimbursement to cover the deficit in the COVID emergency expense accounts.

why_it_matters: Free cash and stabilization reserves are what the town draws on for capital projects and emergencies, so deferring capital spending keeps options open if state aid or tax receipts fall short.
Rising debt service in a later year would take a larger share of the town budget, mostly taxes, so the debt subcommittee's work bears on future tax bills and borrowing decisions.
watch_next: June 11 meeting: review of Town Meeting and the charge to the debt subcommittee.
Next meeting: a second pass through the capital plan for items that must be spent before mid-November.
